title: Put the year down, Maya

loopNote: No loop. This is a duo reel, so it ends on the button (Floey's 'pick the year up' calling back to 'put the year down', then Maya's look to camera) and then the end card.
caption:
Maya's best comparison post still had last year's prices, so she went straight for the year in the title. Floey stopped her.

Google's own helpful content guide lists this as a warning sign: changing a page's date to make it look fresh when the content hasn't really changed.

So do it in this order:
1. Prices and plan names
2. The feature table
3. Only then the year in the title and the Last updated date

January re-dating season is coming. Save this for your next audit.

Which of your comparison posts is still quoting last year's prices? (Maya and Floey are from the Flowra team.)
topic: Your comparison post is going sour: fix the prices and the feature table first, and change the year in the title last
editorNotes: The hook makes Maya look dumb and spoils the payoff. In 'My best post has last year's prices! Quick, change the year.' she knows the prices are wrong and still chooses to just change the date. That is not an instinct, it is covering it up. It also means 'Three prices changed' and 'I nearly stamped this year on wrong prices' tell us nothing new, because she said it in line one. Have her react to what the viewer really notices, the old year on her best post (for example, she sees last year in the title and panics that it looks dead), and let the stale prices be what the check finds. 'Quick, change the year' is also unclear about which year until the title is on screen.

Beat 8's 1.2 second pause cannot hold everything written for it: a cut to wide, Maya typing with its sound, Floey's tilt, a cut to the listInsert, row 1 turning good with a ding, row 2 a ding 0.4 seconds later, and a rise. That is two cuts and four sounds in about a second, which breaks the one-sound-every-0.4-seconds rule and would flash past. Make the pause about 2.8 to 3.2 seconds, or move the typing to the end of Maya's line 7, so each cut and each ding gets its own beat.

Beat 3 asks for the 'maya' shot and also for Floey at the edge of frame tilting her head. In the 'maya' shot Floey is fully out of frame, so the animator cannot draw this. Either use 'wide' (or nudge the shot so Floey is fully in, not sliced) or drop Floey's tilt and put her reaction on the next cut.

The hook pill 'Prices: last checked a year ago (my example)' is a sentence. DUO.stat is a short number pill by her head ('-40%'), so this will overflow or crowd her face in frame one. Use something short like 'Prices: 1 yr old', or put the stale year in the title on the laptop. Leave '(my example)' off the screen in the pill and in row 1's '3 prices changed (my example)': the post is already framed as Maya's own ('My post: ...'), and the extra words read as a legal note and make the value too long.

Beat 2 puts a cut to mayaTight, a jolt, a pose change to rest, a surprised face and a '?' mark into a 0.25 second pause. That is a one-frame flash, and Maya's next line starts on top of her jolt. Lengthen the pause to about 0.7 seconds so her reaction to 'Put the year down' lands. It is the first laugh.

Beat 9, 'I nearly stamped this year on wrong prices', sounds written, not said, and 'on wrong prices' trips in bf_emma's fast delivery. Say it the way a person would, for example 'Oh. I nearly put this year on last year's prices.' That is also the clearer twist line and goes with the fixed hook.

(polish) Row 2 already reads '2 rows out of date' during Floey's tip, before Maya has checked anything. Her 'Two rows wrong' then repeats the screen instead of finding something. Start rows 1 and 2 as 'not checked yet' (bad) and fill in '3 prices changed' and '2 rows out of date' as she says them, so the check visibly happens.

(polish) The brief asks for the reel to end with the three-step checklist on screen. The script holds it for 3.2 seconds and then cuts back to wide for the button. That is fine under the duo rules, but think about bringing the checklist back small behind the end card, or holding it under Floey's button line, since saving is the goal.

(polish) The button 'Now you can pick the year up.' is a neat callback, but it is gentle. It gets a smile, not a send. Maya's 'flat, satisfied look' also clashes with expr happy (pick one: deadpan, or a smug grin). Consider ending on something with more snap, such as the cold coffee joke from the brief (Floey sips, 'You're welcome.'), or Maya changing the year with a defiant, slow single keypress.

(polish) Sound and acting mismatches. In the hook Maya is in pose type from frame one, but the typing sound only starts on 'change the year', so her hands move silently. Start the sound at frame one. The listInsert's first entrance in beat 6 has no whoosh. The rise is used twice (before the payoff and again in the button). Use a click or ding for the year change in the button so the rise stays a single setup.

(polish) Frame one has Maya at expr worried in pose type. The rule asks for her mid-panic in frame one, so use expr panic (or pose panic or cheeks for a beat before she types) to make the hook read in under 2 seconds.

(polish) Small staging points. Beat 2 says Floey 'turns to face Maya', but she is already facing her (facing -1, head turned in the hook), so give her a different move such as a slow lean or a tail flick. In beat 4 Floey takes off and hovers inside the 'floey' shot. floeyHover is by Maya's head, so check she is not sliced at the frame edge, or nudge the shot.
